sourceOccurrences.note: Anisotropic second-moment growth explains the even-kernel logarithm. Coordinate symmetry and harmonicity cancel the quadratic term without requiring a finite full second moment. The stronger power range and explicit obstructions are independent deductions, not new source errors or model-specific spatial estimates.

proofUses.reason: Three spatial regions give the power bounds, with logarithmic endpoints excluded.
A signed summable kernel preserves the leading coefficient; the expansion is phrased additively to include zero total mass.
Evenness of the convolving kernel cancels the first-order Taylor term; exponents and endpoints are explicit.
A single translate has a first-order error; the symmetric pair has a second-order error.
The final convolution retains the 2/d remainder under the stated spatial estimates.
The summable-kernel power bound controls h*g, while evenness, a truncated second moment and a spatial tail split give the boundary logarithm.
Coordinate symmetry makes each truncated covariance scalar, harmonicity cancels its Hessian contraction, and fourth-order Taylor bounds control the remaining near sum.
A nonnegative anisotropic kernel has a logarithmically divergent traceless second moment; an exact nearest-neighbour expansion gives a positive fourth-order coefficient.
